description: Finish HID device enumeration and control for Stream Deck and USB button controllers. Enable configurable button mappings for workout control without touching keyboard/mouse.

phases.name: Device Enumeration & Connection
phases.description: Implement actual HID device enumeration using hidapi library and device lifecycle management

subtasks.title: Implement hidapi device enumeration
subtasks.description: Complete the scan_devices() method in DefaultHidDeviceManager to use hidapi::HidApi for actual device enumeration. Filter for known devices and map them to HidDevice structs.
acceptance_criteria: HidApi::new() is called to initialize the HID API
device_list() is used to enumerate all connected HID devices
Known devices are filtered by vendor_id and product_id
Serial numbers are captured when available
Returns populated Vec<HidDevice> with real device data
subtasks.notes: Implemented scan_devices() using hidapi::HidApi for real device enumeration. Filters for known devices, captures serial numbers, handles duplicates, and updates internal device list.

subtasks.title: Implement device open/close with hidapi handles
subtasks.description: Complete open_device() and close_device() methods to actually open HID device handles using hidapi. Store device handles for later input reading.
acceptance_criteria: Device is opened using HidApi::open(vendor_id, product_id)
Device handle is stored in a HashMap keyed by device UUID
close_device() properly closes the handle and removes from storage
Proper error handling for device not found, permission denied, etc.
subtasks.notes: Implemented open_device() and close_device() methods with actual hidapi integration. Added device_path field for path-based opening. Device handles stored in Arc<Mutex<HashMap<Uuid, hidapi::HidDevice>>>. Uses spawn_blocking for thread-safe hidapi operations. Path-first opening strategy with VID/PID fallback. Proper error handling for permissions and device access issues.

subtasks.title: Implement device monitoring with hotplug detection
subtasks.description: Complete start_monitoring() to spawn a background task that periodically scans for device changes (connect/disconnect) and emits appropriate events.
acceptance_criteria: Background task polls for device changes every 2 seconds
DeviceConnected event emitted when new device detected
DeviceDisconnected event emitted when device removed
Monitoring can be stopped via stop_monitoring()
Thread-safe access to device state
subtasks.notes: Implemented start_monitoring() with background polling task that scans for HID device changes every 2 seconds. Uses identity_key() (VID:PID:Serial or VID:PID:Path) for device tracking across scans. Emits DeviceConnected and DeviceDisconnected events via broadcast channel. Auto-closes device handles on disconnect. Thread-safe with Arc<RwLock> and Arc<Mutex>. Added unit tests for identity_key() method.

subtasks.title: Add auto-reconnect logic for disconnected devices
subtasks.description: Implement automatic reconnection when a previously connected device is unplugged and replugged. Track devices by serial number or VID:PID for identification.
acceptance_criteria: Previously opened devices are tracked by serial number or VID:PID
When device reconnects, it is automatically re-opened
Button mappings are restored on reconnect
DeviceOpened event emitted on successful reconnect
Configurable reconnect delay (default 1 second)
subtasks.notes: Implemented auto-reconnect logic for HID devices. Added auto_reconnect and reconnect_delay_ms config options. Track opened devices by identity key. When device reconnects, auto-reopen after configurable delay (default 1s). Emit DeviceReconnected event on success. Remove from tracking when explicitly closed. Added unit tests for tracking and config.

phases.name: Input Reading & Event Processing
phases.description: Implement reading button presses from HID devices and processing them through the mapping system

subtasks.title: Implement HID input reading task
subtasks.description: Create a background task that reads input reports from open HID devices and translates them to RawButtonEvent structs.
acceptance_criteria: New input.rs module with HidInputReader struct
Non-blocking read loop using device.read_timeout()
Raw HID reports parsed to identify button presses
RawButtonEvent emitted for each button press/release
Handles multiple devices concurrently
subtasks.notes: Implemented HidInputReader with background task that reads input reports from open HID devices. Uses non-blocking read_timeout() with 50ms timeout for responsive multi-device polling. Created HidDeviceType enum for device categorization (StreamDeck, StreamDeckPedal, Generic). Implemented report parsing for all three device types with state tracking to emit only press/release transitions. Added comprehensive unit tests for parsing logic. Exports HidInputReader, HidDeviceType, OpenDeviceInfo, RawButtonEvent from mod.rs.

subtasks.title: Add Stream Deck protocol support
subtasks.description: Implement Stream Deck-specific input report parsing. Stream Deck devices use a custom protocol for button state reporting.
acceptance_criteria: New streamdeck.rs module for Stream Deck protocol
Parse button state report (which button pressed)
Handle button release detection
Support all Stream Deck variants (6, 15, 32 buttons)
Proper button index mapping for each model
subtasks.notes:
Implemented Stream Deck-specific input report parsing with comprehensive support for all models:

- Created new streamdeck.rs module with:
  - StreamDeckModel enum for all variants (Original, Mini, XL, MK.2, Pedal)
  - StreamDeckParser struct for stateful parsing with press/release detection
  - Model-specific button data offset handling (1-byte header for Original/Mini, 4-byte for MK.2/XL)
  - Grid coordinate conversion utilities (button_to_grid, grid_to_button)
  - Human-readable button labels

- Updated input.rs:
  - Added stream_deck_model field to OpenDeviceInfo
  - Automatic model detection from VID/PID
  - Updated parse_streamdeck_report to handle all formats correctly
  
- Added comprehensive unit tests for all Stream Deck models and report formats

Exported StreamDeckModel and StreamDeckParser from mod.rs.

subtasks.title: Add generic USB button controller support
subtasks.description: Implement support for generic USB button controllers that send standard HID gamepad/keyboard reports.
acceptance_criteria: New generic.rs module for standard HID button devices
Parse gamepad-style button reports
Support keyboard-style button devices
Auto-detect report format based on usage page
Map generic button indices to internal codes
subtasks.notes: Created generic.rs module with GenericHidParser supporting four report formats (Bitmap, BytePerButton, KeyboardScanCode, ConsumerControl). Added auto-detection, known device profiles for common foot pedals, and integration with input.rs. Extended OpenDeviceInfo with generic_config and detected_format fields. Comprehensive unit tests included.

subtasks.title: Wire input events through ButtonInputHandler
subtasks.description: Connect the HID input reading to the existing ButtonInputHandler to process raw events and emit mapped actions.
acceptance_criteria: HidInputReader sends RawButtonEvent to ButtonInputHandler
ButtonInputHandler.process_event() is called for each event
ButtonActionEvent emitted when mapping exists
Learning mode captures button codes correctly
subtasks.notes:
Implemented HID input to ButtonInputHandler wiring:

- Added button_handler field to HidInputReader (Option<Arc<DefaultButtonInputHandler>>)
- Added with_button_handler() builder method for integration
- Modified start() to clone button_handler and forward events in the read loop
- Each RawButtonEvent is now sent to both:
  1. The broadcast channel for external subscribers
  2. The ButtonInputHandler.process_event() for mapping lookup and action emission
- Fixed Mutex import consistency (std::sync::Mutex to match device.rs)
- Exported ButtonActionEvent from mod.rs for external consumers
- Added 4 comprehensive tests:
  - test_input_reader_with_button_handler
  - test_input_reader_builder_pattern
  - test_button_handler_receives_events
  - test_learning_mode_captures_button
  - test_learning_mode_ignores_mappings

The complete event pipeline is now: HID device → input reader → raw event → button handler → mapping lookup → action event

phases.name: Action Execution & Integration
phases.description: Implement the action executor and integrate with app systems (workout, audio, fan, etc.)

subtasks.title: Implement DefaultActionExecutor
subtasks.description: Create a concrete implementation of the ActionExecutor trait that handles all ButtonAction types by calling appropriate app subsystems.
acceptance_criteria: New executor.rs module with DefaultActionExecutor
Implements execute() for all ButtonAction variants
Injects dependencies for workout engine, audio, fan controller
Emits ActionResult events via broadcast channel
Handles context checking (ride active, workout active, etc.)
subtasks.notes:
Implemented DefaultActionExecutor in src/hid/executor.rs:

- Generic struct DefaultActionExecutor<A: AudioEngine, F: FanController>
- AppContext struct for ride/workout state tracking
- LapMarker struct for lap time tracking
- ExecutorEvent enum for UI integration (navigation, fullscreen, custom actions)
- NavigationTarget enum for view switching

Handles all ButtonAction types:
- Ride: AddLapMarker, PauseResume, EndRide
- Workout: SkipInterval, ExtendInterval, RestartInterval (RestartInterval is placeholder)
- Audio: VolumeUp, VolumeDown, MuteToggle
- Fan: FanSpeedUp, FanSpeedDown, FanToggle (via MQTT FanController)
- Navigation: ShowMetrics, ShowMap, ShowWorkout, ToggleFullscreen
- Camera: Placeholder for 3D world integration
- Custom: Emit events for external handling

Features: builder pattern for DI, broadcast channels for events, context-aware availability, comprehensive tests.

subtasks.title: Integrate with workout engine for ride/workout actions
subtasks.description: Wire up ride control actions (pause, lap, end) and workout actions (skip interval, extend, restart) to the workout engine.
acceptance_criteria: AddLapMarker triggers ride_recorder.add_lap()
PauseResume toggles ride state
EndRide triggers ride completion flow
SkipInterval calls workout_engine.skip_interval()
ExtendInterval calls workout_engine.extend_interval()
RestartInterval calls workout_engine.restart_interval()
subtasks.notes:
Wired up ride control and workout actions to the workout engine:

- Added restart_segment() method to WorkoutEngine that resets elapsed time to start of current segment
- Added IntervalRestarted event to WorkoutEvent enum for audio/UI notifications
- Added LapMarker struct and lap tracking (add_lap, get_laps, has_laps, lap_count) to RideRecorder
- Wired RestartInterval action in executor to call engine.restart_segment()
- Wired AddLapMarker action to call ride_recorder.add_lap() in addition to internal tracking
- Added 4 comprehensive unit tests for restart_segment functionality

Acceptance criteria met:
- AddLapMarker triggers ride_recorder.add_lap() ✓
- PauseResume toggles ride state (already implemented) ✓
- EndRide triggers ride completion flow (already implemented) ✓
- SkipInterval calls workout_engine.skip_segment() (already implemented) ✓
- ExtendInterval calls workout_engine.extend_segment() (already implemented) ✓
- RestartInterval calls workout_engine.restart_segment() ✓

subtasks.title: Integrate with audio and fan systems
subtasks.description: Wire up audio control actions (volume, mute) and fan control actions (speed, toggle) to their respective subsystems.
acceptance_criteria: VolumeUp/Down adjusts audio engine master volume
MuteToggle toggles audio mute state
FanSpeedUp/Down adjusts fan controller speed
FanToggle toggles fan on/off
Graceful handling when MQTT not connected
subtasks.notes:
Verified and enhanced audio control actions (volume, mute) and fan control actions (speed, toggle) integration with their respective subsystems. The wiring was already implemented in subtask 3.1, but this task added comprehensive tests to verify the integration is working correctly.

Acceptance criteria met:
- VolumeUp/Down adjusts audio engine master volume (via set_volume)
- MuteToggle toggles audio mute state (sets to 0 on mute, restores on unmute)
- FanSpeedUp/Down adjusts fan controller speed (via set_speed)
- FanToggle toggles fan on/off (speed 0 = off, current speed = on)
- Graceful handling when MQTT not connected (MqttError -> ActionError::ExecutionFailed)

Added 16 new integration tests with MockAudioEngine and MockFanController implementations:
- test_volume_up_calls_audio_engine
- test_volume_down_calls_audio_engine
- test_mute_toggle_calls_audio_engine
- test_volume_clamped_at_100/0
- test_fan_speed_up/down_calls_controller
- test_fan_toggle_calls_controller
- test_fan_action_without_controller/profile (graceful error handling)
- test_fan_action_mqtt_error_handling
- test_fan_speed_clamped_at_100/0
- test_fan_speed_up_turns_fan_on

subtasks.title: Integrate with UI navigation

ShowMap switches ride screen to map view
ShowWorkout switches ride screen to workout view
ToggleFullscreen toggles full-screen mode
View changes are reflected immediately in UI

- Wired ExecutorEvent::FullscreenToggle to toggle fullscreen mode
- Exported RideView from ui/screens/mod.rs

Acceptance criteria met:
- ShowMetrics switches ride screen to metrics view ✓
- ShowMap switches ride screen to map view ✓
- ShowWorkout switches ride screen to workout view ✓
- ToggleFullscreen toggles full-screen mode ✓
- View changes are reflected immediately in UI ✓

subtasks.title: Wire HID config persistence to database

Button mappings loaded for each enabled device
Changes from settings screen saved to database
Config survives app restart
subtasks.notes: Created src/hid/persistence.rs with conversion functions between HID runtime types and database storage types. Updated app.rs to load HID config from database on startup and save on settings changes. Added database field to RustRideApp. Registered loaded button mappings with ButtonInputHandler.

subtasks.title: Complete settings screen device scanning
